newsitem.title: USA: Bradys inch higher, sit tight for FOMC decision.
newsitem.headline: Bradys inch higher, sit tight for FOMC decision.

text.p: Most emerging market debt prices edged higher in late U.S. trade on Friday, as yield spreads narrowed by about five basis points over U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
Trading volume was relatively thin, Brady market players said, as they awaited the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decision on U.S. monetary policy at its meeting Tuesday.

"We're a little better bid ... there's some buying and short covering continuing from yesterday," said one Brady trader at a U.S. investment bank. "Other than that, it's been a very quiet day," he said.
In Latin American debt, highly illiquid Ecuador and Peru Brady instruments seemed favorably priced, attracting some interest, Brady traders said.
As the market begins to build confidence in Ecuador, one trader said, "that's when you have to attack."
Ecuador discounts ECIEB=RR jumped 1-1/8 to 67.50 bid and Ecuador PARs rose 5/8 to 43-3/8 bid.
Peru's PDI bonds PEDI=RR rose one percentage point to 61-5/8 bid. One trader cited positive signs in the Peruvian hostage crisis as a possible boost to the market.

The market received news on Friday that the Dominican Republic offered asylum to some members of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), who continue to hold 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's mansion in Peru.
"The government expressed its agreement to receive some of the rebels in Lima" as a way of contributing to a peaceful resolution of the crisis, a Dominican government statement said.
But another Brady trader said market players are hardly yearning for Peru Brady debt. Although Peru PDIs are well-bid, "they are very illiquid, so any sort of flow moves it a lot," he said.
Argentina and Brazil also tightened on the day, traders said.
Argentina PARs AR4C23=RR were up 1/2 to 64-5/8 bid and Argentina discounts AR425C23=RR rose a full point to 82-1/4.
Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR traded up 5/8 to 77-1/8 bid and Brazil PARs BR4D24=RR were up 5/8 to 63-3/4.
In Eastern European emerging debt, Poland PARs PO275024=RR were up 1/8 to 54-1/4 bid and Poland PDIs P0325024=RR were 1/2 higher, to 82 bid.
By late afternoon, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was off 2/32 at 95-25/32 bid, yielding 6.96 percent.
